📝 Assessment report: Word, LaTeX and PDF

Source: vignettes/articles/report.Rmd
report.Rmd
📦 Data: FAO Global Capture Production, release 2026.1.0 (published by FAO on 2026-03-30; catches 1950–2024), downloaded from Capture_2026.1.0.zip. Licence CC BY 4.0. fao_data_info() shows the release you use and how to cite it.

fao_report() writes the assessment report of one FAO major fishing area as a Word file (and, if asked, as LaTeX and PDF), in Chinese or English, in one call. It runs the analyses of the package on the area, writes their results into text made from templates, adds the charts and tables with numbered captions, and lists the references it cites.

fao_report(34)                                                  # language of fao_settings()
fao_report("Atlantic, Eastern Central", lang = "zh", author = "Hongyu Lin")
fao_report(34, lang = "en", font = "Times New Roman", citation = "fao")

The report is a first draft. The parts only the author can write, such as other data sources, the discussion of the conclusions and other references, are marked in grey with “To be completed” (“待补充” in Chinese reports). Check the generated text before you use it.

🚀 A first report 

report <- fao_report(34, file = "FAO34_report_en.docx", lang = "en")
report
#> FAO report: /tmp/RtmpgRZd8i/faofishingreport_site_1bcd1c9c5875/FAO34_report_en.docx
#> Sections: total, species, countries, groups, status, quality, diversity, fleets
#>   $main_species           main species of the last five years (10 rows)
#>   $main_countries         main fishing countries of the last five years (10 rows)
#>   $analyses               results of the analyses: total, species, countries, groups, status, quality, diversity, fleets

The area is given by its code (34) or its English name ("Atlantic, Eastern Central"). The call takes about half a minute and reports its progress in messages (hidden on this page): each analysis, then the file written. Without file, the report is saved as reports/FAO34_report_en.docx in the working directory; on this page the working directory is a temporary folder.

The analyses run in a temporary folder of their own, with charts at 300 dpi and no PowerPoint files. The charts end up in the Word file only, so the report leaves no chart files in your folder; run the analysis functions themselves to keep them (see 🌊 Fishing area analysis).

fao_report() returns the tables of the report invisibly, so assign the result. The main species of the last five years:

show_table(report$main_species, digits = 1)

📑 What the report contains

In this order:

  1. Cover, on its own page without a page number: the project (“Project Report” unless project is given), the title, the report number, the author, the affiliation (only if given) and the date.
  2. Title block: “Report 1” (“报告一” in Chinese reports, with Chinese numerals), the title and the author, centred.
  3. Abstract: one paragraph with the area, the years and release of the FAO data, the topics and methods of the sections switched on, one sentence of results for the total catch, the main species, the main country, the stock status and CMSY++ (when these sections are on), and a closing recommendation.
  4. 1 Data and methods
    • 1.1 Data sources: the FAO Global Capture Production release used, the date FAO published it, the date it was downloaded and the link to the file; the years, and the numbers of countries and species items in the area; the ASFIS list of species, the FAO yearbook of statistics, and how coastal countries are defined. A grey note asks for other data sources (regional fisheries management organisations, national agencies, Sea Around Us, …).
    • 1.2 Methods: one paragraph for each method used by the sections switched on (breakpoints, Mann-Kendall trend tests, stock status plots, diversity indices, …), with its references, and a last paragraph on the software (R and faofishingreport).
  5. 2 Results and conclusions: one numbered subsection (2.1, 2.2, …) for each section switched on, with its text, figures and tables. The last subsection, Conclusions, has one numbered conclusion per section, (1), (2), …, and a grey note asking to complete them with stock assessments, the literature and management measures.
  6. 3 Stock assessment of the main species (CMSY++), with cmsy = TRUE only: an overview, one subsection per species and a summary (see 📉 CMSY++ assessment).
  7. References: the references cited in the text, then a grey note on how to add others.
  8. Appendix: mean yearly catch by decade of the main species (Table A1) and of the main countries (Table A2), and with CMSY++ the reference points, the priors and their sources (Tables A3 to A5).

The grey notes are the paragraphs the author has to write or check: other data sources, the conclusions, other references, the comparison of each CMSY++ assessment with other assessments, and the preferred temperatures of the species of the mean temperature of the catch. If a chart could not be drawn, the report has “[Figure not available]” in its place.

🔎 Inside the Word file

Every paragraph of the report has a named Word style (“FAO Body”, “FAO Heading 1”, …). The format of the whole report can be changed in Word by modifying a style, and the file can be read back in R with the officer package:

word <- officer::docx_summary(officer::read_docx(report$file))
word <- word[word$content_type == "paragraph", ]
table(word$style_name)
#> 
#> FAO Abstract Heading           FAO Author             FAO Body 
#>                    1                    3                   30 
#>          FAO Caption    FAO Cover Project       FAO Cover Text 
#>                   14                    1                   13 
#>      FAO Cover Title           FAO Figure        FAO Heading 1 
#>                    1                   14                    4 
#>        FAO Heading 2             FAO Note        FAO Reference 
#>                   11                    3                   11 
#>    FAO Table Caption       FAO Table Text            FAO Title 
#>                    4                    4                    2

The headings, styles “FAO Heading 1” and “FAO Heading 2”:

outline <- function(word) {
  headings <- word[word$style_name %in% c("FAO Heading 1", "FAO Heading 2"), ]
  cat(paste0(ifelse(headings$style_name == "FAO Heading 2", "    ", ""), headings$text), sep = "\n")
}
outline(word)
#> 1 Data and methods
#>     1.1 Data sources
#>     1.2 Methods
#> 2 Results and conclusions
#>     2.1 Catch trends and stages
#>     2.2 Main species
#>     2.3 Main fishing countries
#>     2.4 Composition by species group
#>     2.5 Stock status
#>     2.6 Data quality
#>     2.7 Diversity and concentration of the catch
#>     2.8 Coastal and distant-water fleets
#>     2.9 Conclusions
#> References
#> Appendix

The abstract, the first “FAO Body” paragraph after the heading “Abstract”:

after_heading <- seq_len(nrow(word)) > which(word$style_name == "FAO Abstract Heading")
abstract <- word$text[after_heading & word$style_name == "FAO Body"][1]
show_table(data.frame(abstract))
abstract
FAO Major Fishing Area 34 (Atlantic, Eastern Central) is one of the important marine fishing areas of the world. Using the FAO Global Capture Production statistics for 1950–2024 (release 2026.1.0), this report analyses the catch trends, the main species, the main fishing countries, the composition of the catch, the status of the stocks, the quality of the data, the diversity of the catch and the catch of coastal and distant-water fleets, with breakpoint analysis, Mann-Kendall trend tests, stock status plots and diversity and concentration indices. In 2024, the catch in the area was 5.10 million t, 6.3% of the world’s marine capture production. The catch peaked in 2018 at 5.52 million t, and the catch of 2024 was 92.4% of the peak. Breakpoints divide the catch series into 4 stages (1950–1968, 1969–1987, 1988–2009 and 2010–2024). In the last five years, European pilchard(=Sardine) was the main species item, with 20.4% of the catch. Morocco was the main fishing country, with 27.7% of the catch of the last five years. In 2024, 36.1% of the stocks were over-exploited or collapsed. Monitoring and assessment of the main stocks, and the reporting of catch at species level, should be strengthened.

🧾 Arguments

Argument Default Meaning
area (required) The FAO major fishing area: its code, e.g. 34, or its English name, e.g. "Atlantic, Eastern Central". An unknown area gives an error that lists the marine areas.
... Settings of the analyses, named with the section as prefix, e.g. species_h_value = 0.2 (see ⚙️ Settings of the analyses)
file reports/FAO<code>_report_<lang>.docx The file to write; its folder is created if needed. The other formats get the same name with .tex and .pdf.
format "docx" One or more of "docx", "latex" and "pdf" (see 🖨️ Word, LaTeX and PDF)
lang NULL: the language of fao_settings() "zh" (Chinese) or "en" (English); "both" gives a Chinese report
title made from the area e.g. “Assessment of Marine Capture Production in FAO Major Fishing Area 34 (Atlantic, Eastern Central)”
report_no 1 Number of the report: “Report 1” (“报告一” in Chinese reports, with Chinese numerals up to 99), and the first number of the figures and tables (Figure 1-1, Table 1-1)
author NULL: “Author” The author on the cover, under the title and in the properties of the file
affiliation NULL: no line The affiliation on the cover
project NULL: “Project Report” The text at the top of the cover (“课题报告” in Chinese reports)
date Sys.Date() The date on the cover, written as YYYY-MM-DD; also the access date in the references to R and faofishingreport
font NULL: “Times New Roman” in Chinese reports, “Arial” in English reports The font of Latin script and numbers; in English reports, of all text
font_zh "FangSong" The Chinese font of the body text, title, tables and references; headings and captions stay in SimHei and KaiTi
citation "apa" Citation style of English reports: "apa" or "fao". Chinese reports always use numbered citations (GB/T 7714).
top_n 10 Number of main species and countries in the tables and charts, and of species assessed with CMSY++ (unless cmsy_top is given)
data_version "latest" The FAO release to use, as in load_fao_data()
total, species, countries, groups, status, quality, diversity, fleets TRUE Sections switched on by default (see 🧩 Sections)
shocks, collapse, synchrony, pelagic, mtc, distant FALSE Sections switched off by default
cmsy FALSE TRUE adds a CMSY++ assessment of the main species; the result of an earlier run can also be given (see 📉 CMSY++ assessment)

🧩 Sections

Each analysis is a section of the report, switched on or off with the argument of the same name. The settings of its function are given with the prefix in the last but one column, and the last column lists the references its text cites (full references at the end of this page).

Switch Default Section of the report Function Prefix References cited
total TRUE Catch trends and stages: total catch with its breakpoints, 10-year trend, share of the world’s marine catch fishing_area_data() total_ Bai and Perron (2003), Zeileis et al. (2003), Mann (1945), Kendall (1975)
species TRUE Main species of the last five years: table, charts, breakpoints and 10-year trends fishing_area_species() species_ as total
countries TRUE Main fishing countries of the last five years: table, charts, map, breakpoints and trends fishing_area_country() countries_ as total
groups TRUE Composition by ISSCAAP species group in the last year species_group_composition() groups_ none
status TRUE Stock status plots stock_status() status_ Kleisner et al. (2013)
quality TRUE Data quality: reported and estimated catch, taxonomic level data_quality() quality_ none
diversity TRUE Diversity and concentration of the catch (Shannon index, HHI) diversity_concentration() diversity_ Shannon (1948), Rhoades (1993)
fleets TRUE Catch of coastal countries and distant-water fleets coastal_distant() fleets_ none
shocks FALSE Catch shocks catch_shocks() shocks_ Cottrell et al. (2019), or Gephart et al. (2017) with shocks_method = "gephart2017"
collapse FALSE Fishery collapses, compared with random series collapse_analysis() collapse_, and collapse_seed Mullon et al. (2005), or Worm et al. (2006) with collapse_method = "worm2006"; Wilberg and Miller (2007)
synchrony FALSE Synchrony of the catch and portfolio effect catch_synchrony() synchrony_ Loreau and de Mazancourt (2008), Thibaut and Connolly (2013), Carlson and Satterthwaite (2011), Ong et al. (2021), Lepš et al. (2019)
pelagic FALSE Pelagic to demersal ratio (P/D) pelagic_demersal() pelagic_ Caddy (1993) and de Leiva Moreno et al. (2000), or Grainger and Garcia (1996) with pelagic_definition = "grainger_garcia"; Hondorp et al. (2010)
mtc FALSE Mean temperature of the catch mean_temperature_catch() mtc_ Cheung et al. (2013), FishBase (Froese and Pauly), Huang et al. (2017) with the ERSST v5 data, Pyper and Peterman (1998), Alajmi et al. (2024)
distant FALSE Profiles of the main distant-water countries in the area distant_water_profile() distant_, and distant_countries Swartz et al. (2010), Garibaldi and Limongelli (2003)
cmsy FALSE Stock assessment of the main species, a part of its own cmsy_area() (and cmsy_input()) cmsy_ Froese et al. (2023), Froese et al. (2017), FishBase (Froese and Pauly), Plummer (2003), FAO (2026b)

Every report also cites the FAO release used, the FAO yearbook of statistics (FAO 2026a), R and faofishingreport. The analyses themselves are described on the other pages of this site: 🌊 Fishing area analysis, 📈 Composition, stock status and trends, 🔍 Data quality, diversity and fleets, 🌡️ Sea temperature and catch temperature and 📉 CMSY++ stock assessment.

The rest of the report follows the sections switched on:

  • the abstract lists their topics and methods, and has a sentence of results for total, species, countries, status and cmsy;
  • 1.2 Methods has the paragraphs of their methods only (groups, quality and fleets need none);
  • the subsections of 2 Results and conclusions and the figures and tables are numbered in the order of the sections, and the conclusions have one item per section;
  • the references list only what the text cites, e.g. Shannon (1948) only with diversity;
  • the appendix has Tables A1 and A2 only with species and countries, and the CMSY++ tables only with cmsy.

The total catch is always analysed, as it gives the data of the area, but its section is written only with total = TRUE.

🎛️ Fewer or more sections

Three sections switched off, the pelagic to demersal ratio switched on, and stock status plots with smoothed catches:

short <- fao_report(34, file = "FAO34_short.docx", lang = "en", quality = FALSE, diversity = FALSE,
                    fleets = FALSE, pelagic = TRUE, status_smooth = TRUE)
short
#> FAO report: /tmp/RtmpgRZd8i/faofishingreport_site_1bcd1c9c5875/FAO34_short.docx
#> Sections: total, species, countries, groups, status, pelagic
#>   $main_species           main species of the last five years (10 rows)
#>   $main_countries         main fishing countries of the last five years (10 rows)
#>   $analyses               results of the analyses: total, species, countries, groups, status, pelagic
short_word <- officer::docx_summary(officer::read_docx(short$file))
outline(short_word)
#> 1 Data and methods
#>     1.1 Data sources
#>     1.2 Methods
#> 2 Results and conclusions
#>     2.1 Catch trends and stages
#>     2.2 Main species
#>     2.3 Main fishing countries
#>     2.4 Composition by species group
#>     2.5 Stock status
#>     2.6 Pelagic to demersal ratio
#>     2.7 Conclusions
#> References
#> Appendix

The results now have six subsections and the conclusions six items. The abstract and the methods name the P/D ratio, and the references have Caddy (1993), de Leiva Moreno et al. (2000) and Hondorp et al. (2010) instead of Shannon (1948) and Rhoades (1993):

show_table(data.frame(reference = short_word$text[short_word$style_name == "FAO Reference"]), n = 30)

The methods paragraphs describe the default settings of each analysis, e.g. the inclusion criteria of the stock status plots and a minimum segment of 15% for the breakpoints. When you change such settings (status_smooth = TRUE, status_min_catch = 10000, species_h_value = 0.2, …), the results follow them; describe the change in 1.2 Methods yourself.

⚙️ Settings of the analyses

The function of each section has its own arguments. Give them to fao_report() with the name of the section and “_” in front: species_h_value = 0.2 is h_value = 0.2 of fishing_area_species(). Your settings win over the values the report sets.

In fao_report() Goes to Effect
species_h_value = 0.2 fishing_area_species(h_value = 0.2) Breakpoints of the main species with a minimum segment of 20% of the series
countries_line_linewidth = 1 fishing_area_country(line_linewidth = 1) Thinner lines in the charts of the countries
status_smooth = TRUE stock_status(smooth = TRUE) 3-year running mean of the catch before the stocks are classified
status_min_catch = 10000 stock_status(min_catch = 10000) Only stocks with a total catch of at least 10 000 t
shocks_method = "gephart2017" catch_shocks(method = "gephart2017") Shocks as defined by Gephart et al. (2017), with its methods text and reference
collapse_method = "worm2006" collapse_analysis(method = "worm2006") Collapses as defined by Worm et al. (2006): methods, results, chart and conclusion change
collapse_seed = 2 the random number generator, before collapse_analysis() Other random series for the null model (default 1, so the report gives the same numbers every time); the random state of the session is restored afterwards
synchrony_by = "country" catch_synchrony(by = "country") Synchrony of the countries instead of the species
pelagic_definition = "grainger_garcia" pelagic_demersal(definition = "grainger_garcia") Groups of Grainger and Garcia (1996)
mtc_version = "builtin" mean_temperature_catch(version = "builtin") The report default: FishBase data bundled with the package, nothing downloaded
mtc_version = "latest" mean_temperature_catch(version = "latest") The latest FishBase release, downloaded if needed
distant_countries = 5 distant_water_profile(), once per country Profiles of the five countries with the largest distant-water catch in the area over the last five years (default 3), or of the countries named, e.g. distant_countries = c("Russian Federation", "Belize")
cmsy_top = 5 cmsy_area(top = 5) Five species assessed with CMSY++ (default top_n)
cmsy_settings = list(n.iter = 100000) cmsy_area(settings = ...) CMSY++ settings, see cmsy_defaults()

collapse_seed and distant_countries are settings of the report itself. The cmsy_ prefix also takes the arguments of cmsy_input(), such as cmsy_min_years. The arguments that the report sets itself (area, area_data, area_name, lang, pptx and table) cannot be given. Settings of a section that is switched off have no effect.

A setting must be named, start with the name of a section, and be an argument of the section’s function. Otherwise fao_report() stops before any analysis is run, and the error lists what is allowed:

fao_report(34, species_h = 0.2)
#> Error:
#> ! fao_report(): species_h would set h, which is not an argument of fishing_area_species(). Its arguments: rank_range, plot, timeseries_analysis, line_width, point_size, point_alpha, point_shape, line_alpha, axis_text_size, axis_title_size, strip_text_size, axis_text_face, axis_title_face, strip_text_face, smooth_method, smooth_linetype, line_linewidth, text_hjust, text_vjust, text_size, text_color, facet_ncol, h_value, ZH
fao_report(34, speceis_h_value = 0.2)
#> Error:
#> ! Unknown argument of fao_report(): speceis_h_value. Settings of an analysis start with its section: total_, species_, countries_, groups_, status_, quality_, diversity_, fleets_, shocks_, collapse_, synchrony_, pelagic_, mtc_, distant_, cmsy_

📐 Format

Chinese reports follow the usual format of Chinese project reports:

Element Format
Page A4, portrait; margins 2.54 cm at top and bottom, 3.17 cm left and right
Body text FangSong for Chinese and Times New Roman for Latin script and numbers, size 12 (小四), line spacing 1.5, first-line indent of two characters, justified
Title block “报告一” and the title in FangSong, size 18 (小二), bold, centred; the author below in size 12
“摘　要” SimHei, size 15 (小三), centred
Section headings (1, 2, …) SimHei, size 14 (四号)
Subsection headings (1.1, 2.1, …) KaiTi, size 14 (四号)
Captions SimHei, size 12 (小四), centred, numbered by report: 图1-1 below the figure, 表1-1 above the table; 附表1 in the appendix
Tables Three-line tables (top and bottom rules of 1.5 pt, a rule of 0.75 pt below the header), FangSong and Times New Roman size 10.5 (五号), single line spacing
Citations Superscript numbers in square brackets, in the order of first citation: [1], [3,4], [5-7] (GB/T 7714)
References Numbered [1], [2], … in the order of citation, GB/T 7714 format, with a hanging indent
Spaces No spaces between Chinese characters and Latin letters or numbers, except after the number of a heading or caption (“2.1 渔获量变化与阶段划分”, “图1-1 …”)
Page numbers Centred in the footer, size 10.5 (五号); none on the cover, 1 on the title page
Cover Project in SimHei size 26 (一号) bold, title size 22 (二号) bold, other lines size 16 (三号)

English reports have the same page, structure, numbering and tables, in one font for all text, Arial unless font is given (e.g. font = "Times New Roman"). Headings are bold, size 14 for sections and 12 for subsections. Captions start with a bold label: “Figure 1-1. Catch in …”, “Table 1-1. Main species items …”. Citations are author-date, in APA style (default) or in the style of FAO publications (citation = "fao").

In both languages, scientific names of species and genera are in italics, in the text and in the tables: Sardina pilchardus, Trachurus spp. (with “spp.” upright). Names of families and higher groups stay upright, e.g. Actinopterygii. Symbols are in italics as well (P < 0.05, H). The grey notes and the references are written as they are, without the Chinese spacing rule.

The headings have outline levels 1 and 2, so they show in the navigation pane of Word and in a table of contents inserted in Word. The title and author are also stored in the properties of the file.

🖨️ Word, LaTeX and PDF

format chooses the files to write: "docx" (default), "latex" and "pdf", one or more. The analyses run once, and all formats have the same text, figures, tables, captions and references.

fao_report(34, lang = "zh", format = c("docx", "pdf"))      # Word and PDF
fao_report(34, lang = "en", format = "latex")                # the LaTeX source only
report <- fao_report(34, format = c("docx", "latex", "pdf"))
report$file                                                  # named docx, latex and pdf
format Files written (for fao_report(34, lang = "zh")) What it is
"docx" reports/FAO34_report_zh.docx The Word file described in this article
"latex" reports/FAO34_report_zh.tex and the folder reports/FAO34_report_zh_figures/ The XeLaTeX source of the same report, with its figures as PNG files. Chinese reports use the ctexart class, English reports the article class.
"pdf" reports/FAO34_report_zh.pdf (and the .tex) The LaTeX source compiled with XeLaTeX, with bookmarks for the headings

The LaTeX version follows the format of the Word file (see 📐 Format): A4 pages with the same margins, the same fonts and sizes, line spacing 1.5, three-line tables (booktabs, single line spacing, columns sized to their contents and running over pages), numbered captions, the cover without page number and pages numbered from 1 on the title page. The fonts are those installed on the computer:

Windows macOS Linux
Chinese body text (仿宋) FangSong STFangsong FandolFang (TeX Live)
Chinese headings and captions (黑体) SimHei Heiti SC FandolHei
Chinese subsection headings (楷体) KaiTi Kaiti SC FandolKai
Latin text and numbers font: Times New Roman in Chinese reports, Arial in English reports (else Liberation Serif or Sans, else Latin Modern)

Chinese fonts have no bold face: as in Word, bold Chinese text (the titles) is made by thickening the strokes.

Compiling. With the tinytex package (install.packages("tinytex"), then tinytex::install_tinytex() if you have no LaTeX), the PDF is made with tinytex::latexmk(engine = "xelatex"), which installs missing LaTeX packages (ctex, xeCJK, booktabs, longtable, needspace, xurl, …) on the first run. Without tinytex, xelatex must be on the system path. To change the text of the LaTeX version, edit the .tex file and compile it again, e.g. tinytex::xelatex("reports/FAO34_report_zh.tex").

If tinytex cannot install a package because your TeX Live is older than the online repository (“Local TeX Live (2024) is older than remote repository”), update TeX Live (tinytex::reinstall_tinytex()), or install the packages from the archive of your TeX Live year: tlmgr --repository https://ftp.math.utah.edu/pub/tex/historic/systems/texlive/2024/tlnet-final install ctex.

🔖 Citations and references

The references are listed only when the text cites them. The FAO release used, R and faofishingreport are made from the data and the R session (release, publication and access dates, versions); FishBase is cited with the version used when the report has CMSY++ or the mean temperature of the catch; all other references come from inst/extdata/report_references.csv.

Style Citation in the text List of references
Chinese reports, GB/T 7714 superscript [7] in the order of citation, numbered
citation = "apa", APA 7th edition (Kleisner et al., 2013); (Bai & Perron, 2003; Zeileis et al., 2003) alphabetical; same authors and year as 2026a, 2026b
citation = "fao", FAO publications (Kleisner et al., 2013); (Bai and Perron, 2003) alphabetical; same authors and year as 2026a, 2026b

The same two references in each style, as the report writes them (FAO release 2026.1.0, downloaded on 10 October 2026):

Style Kleisner et al. (2013) FAO data
GB/T 7714 Kleisner K, Zeller D, Froese R, et al. Using global catch data for inferences on the world’s marine fisheries[J]. Fish and Fisheries, 2013, 14(3): 293-311. DOI: 10.1111/j.1467-2979.2012.00469.x. FAO. FishStat: Global capture production 1950–2024 (release 2026.1.0)[DB/OL]. Rome: FAO, 2026[2026-10-10]. https://www.fao.org/fishery/static/Data/Capture_2026.1.0.zip.
APA Kleisner, K., Zeller, D., Froese, R., & Pauly, D. (2013). Using global catch data for inferences on the world’s marine fisheries. Fish and Fisheries, 14(3), 293–311. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-2979.2012.00469.x FAO. (2026). FishStat: Global capture production 1950–2024 (Release 2026.1.0) [Data set]. https://www.fao.org/fishery/static/Data/Capture_2026.1.0.zip
FAO Kleisner, K., Zeller, D., Froese, R. & Pauly, D. 2013. Using global catch data for inferences on the world’s marine fisheries. Fish and Fisheries, 14(3): 293–311. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-2979.2012.00469.x FAO. 2026. FishStat: Global capture production 1950–2024 (release 2026.1.0). [Accessed on 10 October 2026]. In: FishStatJ. Available at: https://www.fao.org/fishery/statistics/software/fishstatj/en. Licence: CC-BY-4.0.

In GB/T 7714, the letter in square brackets gives the type of document: [J] journal article, [M] book, [C] proceedings, [R] report, [DB/OL] online database, [CP/OL] online computer program; up to three authors are listed, more as the first three and “et al.”. The FAO style follows the reference lists of FAO publications (e.g. FAO 2024), and cites FishStat data as these publications do, with the access date, FishStatJ and the licence.

📉 CMSY++ assessment

With cmsy = TRUE, the main species are also assessed with CMSY++ (cmsy_area()): the top_n species items identified to species with the largest catch of the last ten years, or cmsy_top of them. CMSY++ needs JAGS, installed once with cmsy_setup(); without it, fao_report() stops with a message. The assessment takes a few minutes.

cmsy_setup()                          # once: JAGS and the R packages of CMSY++
report <- fao_report(34, lang = "en", cmsy = TRUE)
report
#> FAO report: .../reports/FAO34_report_en.docx
#> Sections: total, species, countries, groups, status, quality, diversity, fleets, cmsy
#>   $main_species           main species of the last five years (10 rows)
#>   $main_countries         main fishing countries of the last five years (10 rows)
#>   $cmsy_reference_points  CMSY++ biological reference points with 95% confidence limits (10 rows)
#>   $cmsy_priors            CMSY++ priors, their sources and links (10 rows)
#>   $cmsy                   CMSY++ result (folder .../reports/cmsy/Atlantic__Eastern_Central)
#>   $analyses               results of the analyses: total, species, ..., fleets, cmsy

View(report$cmsy_reference_points)    # r, k, MSY, Fmsy, Bmsy, B/Bmsy and F/Fmsy with 95% limits
View(report$cmsy_priors)              # priors, their sources and links

# 15 main species and countries in the tables, 5 species assessed, longer MCMC chains
fao_report(34, lang = "en", top_n = 15, cmsy = TRUE, cmsy_top = 5,
           cmsy_settings = list(n.iter = 100000))

The report then has an abstract sentence on the stocks, a methods paragraph on CMSY++, and a part of its own after the results:

3 Stock assessment of the main species (CMSY++)
    3.1 Overview
    3.2 European pilchard(=Sardine) (Sardina pilchardus)
    3.3 Round sardinella (Sardinella aurita)
    ...
    3.12 Summary
  • Overview: how many species were assessed (and which could not be), how many stocks were maximally sustainably fished (B/Bmsy ≥ 0.8) or overfished (B/Bmsy < 0.8) in their last year, as in FAO (2026b), and how many lay in the green (B/Bmsy ≥ 1 and F/Fmsy ≤ 1) and red (B/Bmsy < 1 and F/Fmsy > 1) quadrants of the Kobe plot; a table of the results (years, r, k, MSY, B/Bmsy, F/Fmsy, status), the Kobe plot and B/Bmsy of all stocks.
  • One subsection per species: r, k and MSY with their 95% confidence limits, B/Bmsy and F/Fmsy in the last year, the catch as a percentage of MSY, the status, the probabilities of the four Kobe quadrants, the CMSY++ chart of the species, and a grey note asking to compare the result with other assessments and discuss the priors.
  • Summary, and in the appendix: Table A3 biological reference points (r, k, MSY, Fmsy, Bmsy, B/Bmsy, F/Fmsy) with 95% confidence limits, Table A4 the priors (resilience, ranges of r and k, B/k priors of the first, an intermediate and the last year) and Table A5 their sources (source of the r prior, source of the B/k priors, FishBase or SeaLifeBase page of the species), followed by the links to the FishBase data, the CMSY++ code and user guide, and the FAO data.

All CMSY++ results (input files, runs, charts and tables) are kept in the folder cmsy/ next to the report, e.g. reports/cmsy/Atlantic__Eastern_Central/, with cmsy_result.rds. To write the report again, e.g. with other sections or after editing the templates, give that result to cmsy instead of TRUE; CMSY++ does not run again and the cmsy_ settings are not used. The result of cmsy_area() can be given in the same way:

cmsy34 <- readRDS(file.path("reports", "cmsy", "Atlantic__Eastern_Central", "cmsy_result.rds"))
fao_report(34, lang = "en", cmsy = cmsy34, pelagic = TRUE)

area34 <- cmsy_area("Atlantic, Eastern Central", top = 10)
fao_report(34, lang = "en", cmsy = area34)

The charts of the CMSY++ part come from the run, in the language it was run in. See 📉 CMSY++ stock assessment for the method, its settings and its limits: FAO data have catches only, so the results are indicative.

📦 What fao_report() returns

A list of class fao_report, returned invisibly:

Element Content
file Paths of the files written, named docx, latex and pdf
sections The sections switched on
main_species Main species of the last five years: name in the report language, English and scientific names, mean yearly catch (t), share of the catch (%), peak year, catch of the last year as % of the peak, 10-year trend (“up”, “down” or “none”)
main_countries The same for the main fishing countries
mtc_species With mtc = TRUE: the species of the mean temperature of the catch, their FishBase matches and preferred temperatures
analyses The result of each analysis, named by section, e.g. analyses$status is the result of stock_status()
cmsy With CMSY++: the full result of cmsy_area()
cmsy_reference_points With CMSY++: one row per stock with r, k, MSY, Fmsy, Bmsy, B/Bmsy and F/Fmsy, each with its lower and upper 95% confidence limits (_lcl, _ucl), the last catch, the probabilities of the Kobe quadrants and the status
cmsy_priors With CMSY++: resilience and its source, prior ranges of r and k, the MSY prior, the B/k priors with their sources, and links to the species page in FishBase or SeaLifeBase, the FishBase data, the CMSY++ user guide and the FAO data 
names(report)

✏️ Change the wording

All the text of the report comes from inst/extdata/report_text.csv, one row per piece of text with the columns key, en and zh:

texts <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "report_text.csv", package = "faofishingreport"),
                  fileEncoding = "UTF-8", colClasses = "character")
nrow(texts)
#> [1] 269
show_table(data.frame(texts[texts$key %in% c("h_status", "status_p2", "concl_status"), ], row.names = NULL))
key en zh
h_status Stock status 资源开发状态
status_p2 Stock status plots rely on catch data only: a falling catch may also result from management measures, markets or changes in reporting {cite:kleisner2013}, so the results show the general state of exploitation and do not replace stock assessments. 需要指出的是，资源开发状态图仅基于渔获量数据，渔获量的下降也可能源于管理措施、市场需求或统计方式的变化{cite:kleisner2013}，其结果仅反映资源开发的大致状况，不能替代基于资源评估模型的结论。
concl_status In {last_year}, {oc_pct}% of the stocks were over-exploited or collapsed. {last_year} 年处于过度开发和崩溃状态的资源占 {oc_pct}%。
  • {last_year}, {oc_pct}, … are placeholders, filled in with the results. Keep to the placeholders of the original text: an unknown one stops the report with an error.
  • {cite:kleisner2013} cites a reference by its key, {cite:bai2003,zeileis2003} several. It becomes a superscript number in Chinese reports and “(Kleisner et al., 2013)” in English reports.
  • *...* is written in italics (*P*, scientific names), ^...^ as superscript and ~...~ as subscript, e.g. HHI = ∑(100*p*~i~)^2^.

The references are in inst/extdata/report_references.csv:

refs <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "report_references.csv", package = "faofishingreport"),
                 fileEncoding = "UTF-8", colClasses = "character")
show_table(refs[, c("key", "type", "author", "year", "title")], n = 5)
key type author year title
fao_yearbook M FAO 2026 Fishery and Aquaculture Statistics – Yearbook 2024
bai2003 J Bai, J.; Perron, P. 2003 Computation and analysis of multiple structural change models
zeileis2003 J Zeileis, A.; Kleiber, C.; Krämer, W.; Hornik, K. 2003 Testing and dating of structural changes in practice
kleisner2013 J Kleisner, K.; Zeller, D.; Froese, R.; Pauly, D. 2013 Using global catch data for inferences on the world’s marine fisheries
mann1945 J Mann, H. B. 1945 Nonparametric tests against trend
Column Content
key The key used in {cite:key}
type J journal article, M book, C paper in proceedings, R report in a series (e.g. FAO Fisheries Technical Paper). DB (database) and CP (computer program) are the types of the references the function makes itself: the FAO data, FishBase, R and faofishingreport.
author Persons as “Family, I. I.” separated by “;”, or an organisation such as FAO
year, title Year and title
container Journal or proceedings
volume, issue, pages Volume, issue and pages, e.g. 293-311
edition Number of the edition, e.g. 4 for “4th ed.”
series Series of a report or book, e.g. “FAO Fisheries Technical Paper No. 359”
place, publisher Place and publisher
doi, url DOI without “https://doi.org/”, and web address

To change the wording or add references, edit these files in the package source and reinstall the package (e.g. R CMD INSTALL . in the source folder), then restart R: the files are read once per session.
